title: Fibre dimension in a proper flat finitely presented family of spaces
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to T$ be a flat proper finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; finite presentation also requires quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness (the diagonal is quasi-compact). Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed: the representable diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test; finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; universally closed means closed on underlying point spaces, with the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], after every algebraic-space base change. These are the algebraic-space versions of the scheme conventions [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For $t\in T$, let $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its dimension is the supremum of dimensions of affine etale charts over the fibre, with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$; for a scheme this is its topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then
$$n_f:|T|\to\{-\infty,0,1,2,\ldots\},\qquad t\mapsto\dim X_t$$
is locally constant. For every morphism of schemes $h:T'\to T$, if $f':X\times_TT'\to T'$ is the base change, then $n_{f'}=n_f\circ|h|$. In particular the assertion includes arbitrary residue-field extensions, and for every integer $d\geq0$ the locus $\{t:\dim X_t=d\}$ is open and closed and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change. No nonemptiness, pure-dimensionality or connectedness hypothesis on the fibres is required.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] to base change the three hypotheses to any field-valued point of $T$; every such fibre $Y$ is separated and of finite type. We compare its chart dimension with $\dim|Y|$. Use [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] to choose an atlas $W=\coprod_iU_i\to Y$ with $U_i$ affine. The summands are clopen by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]; their inclusions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and their maps to $Y$ are etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. By [lem-sfb-space-etale-atlas-topological-dimension], applied to $f$ and this field-valued base change, $\dim|Y|=\dim W$. Directly from [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], $\dim W=\sup_i\dim U_i$: the largest irreducible closed member of a finite chain lies in one clopen summand, and conversely a chain in a summand is a chain in $W$. For any other affine etale chart $V\to Y$, the coproduct $V\amalg W$ also maps surjectively and etale to $Y$: after a scheme test the two clopen summands are etale, so flatness, unramifiedness and local finite presentation hold locally at every point by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. This atlas gives $\dim(V\amalg W)=\dim|Y|$, while [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone] gives $\dim V\leq\dim(V\amalg W)$. Thus the supremum over all affine charts is exactly $\dim|Y|$. The empty case is the supremum of empty charts, hence $-\infty$. This comparison holds for the ordinary fibres and for all their field extensions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-space-fibre-dimension-lower-semicontinuous] to the given flat finitely presented $f$ and [lem-sfb-proper-space-fibre-dimension-upper-semicontinuous] to the given proper $f$. Both use the chart dimension defining $n_f$; in particular its values are finite integers or $-\infty$. If $n_f(t)=d\geq0$, the intersection $\{n_f>d-1\}\cap\{n_f\leq d\}$ is an open neighbourhood of $t$ on which $n_f=d$. If $n_f(t)=-\infty$, the open neighbourhood $\{n_f\leq-1\}$ consists entirely of empty fibres. Hence $n_f$ is locally constant. Every level set is open, and its complement is the union of all other level sets, so it is also closed. The threshold $-1$ in both cited statements treats dimension zero and emptiness without any nonempty-fibre assumption.

Let $h:T'\to T$, let $t'\in T'$, and put $t=h(t')$. The local residue-field map gives $\kappa(t)\to\kappa(t')$ [def-weil-residue-field]. The fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies
$$ (X\times_TT')_{t'}\simeq X_t\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t'). $$
Explicitly, a point of either sheaf on a test scheme is a map to $X$ and a map to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t')$ with equal composites to $T$; the map to $T'$ is forced by the latter. These identifications preserve both projections. Apply the current statement of [lem-sfb-space-field-extension-dimension] with $k=\kappa(t)$, $K=\kappa(t')$ and $Y=X_t$. Its separated finite-type hypotheses follow from [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Its $Y_K$ is the sheaf fibre product just identified, using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; the scheme fibre-product convention applies to the spectra. It gives $\dim|Y_K|=\dim|X_t|$, including emptiness. By the first step these are their chart dimensions. Thus $n_{f'}(t')=n_f(h(t'))$ pointwise. The same locality node ensures $f'$ is again proper, flat and finitely presented.

For each $d\geq0$, the pointwise equality in the preceding step gives $\{t':n_{f'}(t')=d\}=|h|^{-1}(\{t:n_f(t)=d\})$. This is equality of the open-and-closed loci with their induced open subspaces. Inverse images of open-and-closed sets are open and closed. Taking $T'=\operatorname{Spec}K$ for any field extension of a residue field gives the asserted invariance for arbitrary such extensions. The arguments never require the fibres to be nonempty, connected or pure-dimensional.

lean.statement: theorem proper_flat_fp_fibreDimension_isLocallyConstant_and_baseChange {S : Scheme.{u}} {T : Over S} {X : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace T) (hflat : MapIsFlat f) (hproper : MapIsProper f) (hfp : MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact f.hom.hom ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal f.hom.hom)) : (∀ t : T.left, fibreDimension f t = ⊥ ∨ ∃ d : ℕ, fibreDimension f t = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧ IsLocallyConstant (fibreDimension f) ∧ (∀ d : ℕ, IsClopen {t : T.left | fibreDimension f t = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)}) ∧ (∀ (T' : Over S) (h : T' ⟶ T), fibreDimension (enlargedFibreProductFst (ObjectProperty.homMk ⟨yoneda.map h⟩ : schemeSpace T' ⟶ schemeSpace T) f) = fibreDimension f ∘ h.left) ∧ (∀ (T' : Over S) (h : T' ⟶ T) (d : ℕ), {t' : T'.left | fibreDimension (enlargedFibreProductFst (ObjectProperty.homMk ⟨yoneda.map h⟩ : schemeSpace T' ⟶ schemeSpace T) f) t' = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)} = h.left ⁻¹' {t : T.left | fibreDimension f t = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)})
